text:
alex: quick thread — drafting the PRD for Dedicated capacity autoscale + SLA tradeoffs. want to lock scope before EOW. key questions: target latency SLOs vs cost headroom, warm pool sizing, and fallback model policy.
tamar: thanks alex. can you list the concrete acceptance criteria you're aiming for? makes it easier to validate with infra.
alex: initial thoughts:
- SLA: p95 latency <= 150ms for text-gen (512 tokens) under committed throughput.
- Throughput sizing: commit tiers of 100qps / 500qps / 2000qps per reserved pool.
- Autoscale: primary policy should scale nodes horizontally with target utilization 60% CPU/GPU, plus burst headroom for 30s.
- Warm pool: keep N prewarmed workers per pool equal to max(2, floor(0.05 * committed_capacity_qps)).
- Fallback: if latency SLO violated for >2min, route to cheaper model variant (quantized) with graded quality warning.
- Acceptance tests: synthetic replay at 10x to validate p95, and customer can validate with their trace.
jin: 150ms p95 seems aggressive for 512 tokens on current gpus for some models (e.g., llama-2-70b-instruct). do we mean p95 per-token or total response?
alex: total response (end-to-end server-side). we can scope to our curated "fast" cohort of models for that SLO, and provide separate tiers for heavy models. i.e., SLO applies only to models on the "low-latency" catalog.
maria: for autoscale, warm pool formula above is fine but we should add a cooldown: scale-down only after 5m of sustained low utilization to avoid thrash. scale-up should allow small fast increments for spikes (5–30s).
kevin: ops perspective: need to capture cost impact in PRD. prewarmed workers add steady cost — show a cost delta table per tier (example: 100qps tier +2 prewarmed -> +$X/day). also need safety valve for noisy-tenant mitigation (per-tenant max concurrency).
alex: noted — will add cost table and per-tenant concurrency limits.
sam_cs: from CS: some enterprise customers want guaranteed tail latency even for large models and are willing to pay. can we support dedicated "guaranteed" pools that pin capacity to model-specific VM shapes?
jin: technical note: pinning per-model shapes affects bin-packing. Might need separate rack/instance-type commitments. That should be a separate feature flag in PRD.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: add observability metrics: p50/p95/p99, queue-length, warm-pool-usage, model-fallback-rate, scaledown-events.
maria: edge cases to call out in PRD: sudden cold start after scale-to-zero, model-eviction when memory pressure, promoted job storms from long-tail customers. include acceptance criteria for graceful degradation (e.g., fallback within 30s).
kevin: what about autoscale policy when KV caches need repopulation? scaling up many workers may cause cache-miss storms and higher latency for first requests. we should stage warmup: bring small fraction online, let them ingest common prefixes, then ramp.
alex: good call. add staged rollout: bring 10% workers, wait 20s, then continue. include metrics for cache-warmth (kv_hit_rate).
tamar: for launch criteria:
- doc: PRD signed off by product/eng/ops/cs
- acceptance: load test passes p95 target at committed throughput + 20% margin
- canary: serve 1% traffic for 24h with no regressions, rollback criteria defined
- billing: price table updated and legal approval for reserved contracts
- runbook: oncall playbook for noisy tenants + fallback escalation path
jin: add integration test: simulate model-fallback path and ensure downstream clients receive structured warning header so apps can handle lower-quality responses.
sam_cs: include migration plan for customers currently on shared hosted API to opt into reserved pools. we need a communication template.
alex: next steps: i'll update PRD draft with: cost delta table, staged warmup algorithm, clear SLO scoping by model cohort, acceptance test harness, and canary rollout plan. please review by Thu COB. if no objections we lock scope Fri morning for eng sprint planning.
maria: ack, will review infra implications and sketch implementation plan.
kevin: i'll work on cost numbers and noisy-tenant limits.
sam_cs: i'll draft customer comms + migration template.
tamar: allocating review owners: product (alex/tamar), infra (maria/jin), ops (kevin), cs (sam_cs).
alex: thanks all. ping me if any blockers. :thumbsup:
